full_judgment: 2. The facts necessary to dispose this appeal are that the appellants and respondent Nos. 3 and 4 as the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 612 of 1977 in the Court of Munsif, third Court, Narail (now the Assistant Judge) for declaration of title to the suit land on the averment that the suit land originally belonged to Abhoy Charan Bhattacharay and Prabol Chandra Bhattacharaya, two full brothers under erstwhile landlords, Babu Dhirendra Nath Roy and others at a jama of Rs. 13/1/3 paisa and was recorded and finally published in their names in CS Khatian No. 348 of mouza Bhowakhali. Subsequently, Abhoy Charan Bhattacharaya died leaving behind his only son, Manindra Nath Bhattacharaya who also died unmarried leaving behind his uncle Prabol Charan Bhattacharaya as his heir and thus, Prabol Charan became the sixteen annas owner of the suit land. Prabol Charan later died leaving behind his only son, Harendra Nath Bhattacharaya as his heir who had been impleaded in the suit as pro-forma defendant No. 3. Harendra Nath Bhattacharaya gave oral settlement of the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs on 7th Magh, 1355 BS corresponding to 21-10-1949 on receipt of an amount of Rs.1,500 as salami at an annual rental of Rs. 10-00 and granted receipts for those. Ever since the settlement, the plaintiffs had all along been in continuous and peaceful possession of the suit land for long over twelve years and thus, had also acquired statutory title by adverse possession. During the last rent roll operation, the suit land was wrongly recorded in the names of Harendra Nath Bhattacharaya and deceased Manindra Nath and in such circumstances, the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 204 of 1976 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Narail and the suit was decreed ex-parte in their favour. Thereafter, on the basis of the said decree, the plaintiffs went to mutate their names by filing an application before the Circle Officer (Revenue), Narail and from the report of the Tashilder concerned, as submitted to the Circle Officer (Revenue), it came to the light for the first time that the suit land was enlisted as enemy property. The defendants had no title or possession in the suit land but out of greed of grabbing the suit land, they filed Miscellaneous Case No. 367 of 1969 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Narail under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (the Act, 1950), but when the plaintiffs, on being added as parties, filed written objection, the defendants had created two forged kabalas, purportedly form Harendra Nath Bhattacharaya and Manindra Nath Bhattacharaya through false personation. The former had left this country and settled in India long ago and the latter died long ago. Late Manindra Nath and Harendra Nath were railway employees in India and never executed the kabalas. When the plaintiffs on the basis of the decrees obtained by them, went to mutate their names and filed an application for that purpose, they came to learn that in the meantime, defendant Nos. 1 and 2 had managed to get their names mutated on the strength of their forged kabalas and the Circle Officer (Revenue), Narail refused to allow the mutation in the names of the plaintiffs on 2-11-1977 and being emboldened thereby, defendant Nos. 1 and 2 on 8-11-1977 denied lawful title of the plaintiffs in the suit land, giving rise to the plaintiffs' cause of action and hence the suit.
